https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2026/10/13/oz/.body: Photo: Press service of the president President of Uzbekistan proposes new economic philosophy “O‘Z” President Shavkat Mirziyoyev called for a stop to distinguishing between foreign and domestic investors, saying that “capital, advanced ideas and honest work have no nationality”. He proposed a new economic philosophy called “O‘Z” and assured investors that their businesses would be protected. На русском языке Ўзбек тилида O‘zbek tilida Yesterday, 23:18 Politics President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke out against distinguishing between foreign and domestic investors at a meeting with entrepreneurs and investors in New Tashkent o n 12 October . “Capital, advanced ideas and honest work have no nationality!” the president said. Mirziyoyev proposed a new philosophy for Uzbekistan’s economy called “O‘Z” (first two letters of the country’s name). According to him, it combines the concepts of “Uzbekistan” ( O‘zbekiston ), “change” ( O‘zgarish ), “identity” ( O‘zlik ) and “responsibility” ( Mas’uliyat ). The president stressed that everyone who invests in Uzbekistan, introduces modern technologies and creates jobs contributes to the country’s overall development, regardless of where they come from. Advertising on Gazeta “Anyone who builds New Tashkent or Shirin (a new development in Samarkand — ed. ) together with us is truly one of us!” the head of state said. He also assured investors that their property and businesses would be protected by the law, the state and the president personally. Talking to investors, Mirziyoyev said that the proposals raised at the meeting would be considered. He said he would visit New Tashkent again in one month to check how instructions are being implemented. He called on investors and entrepreneurs to unite around a new slogan: “Our own idea! Our own investments! Our own future! New Uzbekistan, New Tashkent — they are ours!” Mirziyoyev expressed confidence that New Tashkent would see the implementation of numerous unique projects of national importance. On Monday, the president attended a ceremony marking the launch of seven facilities worth $1 billion and the start of construction on 10 projects worth $2.5 billion in New Tashkent. These include residential complexes, infrastructure and business facilities, a park on the banks of the Chirchiq river, a central hospital and a school. Investors in New Tashkent will be exempt from the requirement to landscape 30% of the land plots they purchase, with the state ensuring that 30% of the city’s territory is greened. The costs of green certification will also be reimbursed for non-residential projects worth more than $50 million. Major investors will receive individual assistance. At the same meeting, Mirziyoyev instructed officials to simplify the implementation of investment projects in New Tashkent. Infrastructure fees for businesses will be reduced threefold to tenfold. Land will also be allocated through the Swiss Challenge mechanism. The city’s master plan may be adjusted to accommodate investors' proposals. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/10/14/taji.body: Governance News Tajikistan Tajikistan’s labor minister orders stricter oversight of timely wage payments Solekha Kholmakhmadzoda also called for stepped-up efforts to employ citizens within the country and to support migrants returning home. Nigora Bukhorizade , asia+ 14.10.2026 13:55 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL Tajikistan’s Minister of Labour, Migration and Employment Solikha Kholmakhmadzoda has instructed officials to strengthen oversight of timely wage payments and the protection of workers’ rights. These issues were among those discussed on 13 October at a collegium meeting of the ministry devoted to the results of its work over the first nine months of 2026. As the Ministry of Labour , Migration and Employment reports, the meeting was attended by the heads of the Migration Service, the Agency for Labour and Employment, the State Labour, Migration and Employment Inspectorate, and the ministry’s representative office in Russia. Particular attention was paid to compliance with labour legislation, the protection of workers’ rights, timely payment of wages, workplace safety, and the prevention of industrial accidents. Labour migration was discussed as a separate agenda item. Specifically, the meeting addressed expanding the geography of employment for Tajik citizens abroad, developing organised recruitment of workers for foreign employers, and improving conditions for labour migrants. Support for citizens returning from labour migration was also named as a priority. The minister instructed officials to step up efforts to find them employment and create income opportunities within the country. ‹ › The meeting also reviewed the implementation of vocational training programmes, employment promotion initiatives, and craft development schemes. Deputy Minister Sharif Norzoda delivered a report on the ministry’s performance over the nine months. He presented the results of the department’s work, the progress of state programmes, and issues requiring additional attention. Following the meeting, Solikha Kholmakhmadzoda gave the heads of the ministry’s divisions specific instructions to address identified shortcomings, strengthen oversight of sectoral programme implementation, and improve operational efficiency. The minister demanded that the assigned tasks be completed on time and that the necessary measures be taken to resolve existing problems. Join us on social media! https://24.kg/en/article/two-potential-p.body: Two potential candidates in Kyrgyzstan’s upcoming presidential election have taken the state language proficiency test, Batma Topoeva-Stavitskaya, head of Kyrgyztest state institution, told 24.kg news agency . She said the names of those who took the test and their results would not be disclosed in accordance with established procedures. The state language proficiency requirements for presidential candidates have not changed ahead of the upcoming election. All prospective candidates take the standard test. Kyrgyzstan’s next presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027. President Sadyr Japarov has publicly announced his intention to run. Former Interior Minister and politician Omurbek Suvanaliev, as well as former prosecutor and ex-head of the Financial Police Syimyk Zhapykeev, have also announced plans to run.

https://24.kg/en/article/kyrgyzstan-is-b.body: Citizens of Kyrgyzstan recruited by Russia to take part in the military operation in Ukraine can be brought home if they seek assistance in advance. Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev said this in response to a lawmaker’s question at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration. Earlier, MP Aibek Altynbekov said that a Kyrgyz citizen in Russia had been forced to sign documents before a court ruling was issued and taken to a training camp. However, he did not provide further details about the man. Kulubaev said the Foreign Ministry was actively working to address the issue. "If we learn that Kyrgyz citizens are being drawn into hostilities, we manage to stop the process. Sometimes they are summoned to military enlistment offices or taken straight to a pretrial detention facility, forced to sign documents and taken away. When we learn about such cases, we manage to intervene and help many migrants. However, some leave without informing anyone. We only find out after they have left, when their parents learn what happened and contact us. Citizens can file an application, after which, through our embassy in Ukraine, we try to contact them and secure their release,” he said. Jeenbek Kulubaev added that many citizens do not report such cases, and the Foreign Ministry often learns about them only after the individuals are wounded or killed. "Sometimes even their parents know nothing. Once a person has gone to war, it becomes much more difficult to bring them back. If we know which military unit they are in and where they are stationed, we make efforts to help,” he said. The foreign minister did not disclose how many Kyrgyz citizens had been brought home from the war.

https://www.azernews.az/nation/265517.ht.body: Hizb ut-Tahrir links emerge after hijab protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara 14 October 2026 00:53 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Footage of a protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara over alleged restrictions on the hijab was first circulated by a media platform linked to the Islamist organisation Hizb ut-Tahrir, according to Azerbaijani media reports. Musavat.com investigated the platform, Köklü Değişim Medya, after it published the first footage of the demonstration on its X account, Turkustan.az reported. According to the investigation, Köklü Değişim Medya and Köklü Değişim Dergisi belong to the Turkish representation of Hizb ut-Tahrir. Hizb ut-Tahrir, whose name translates from Arabic as the “Party of Liberation”, is an international pan-Islamist and fundamentalist political organisation founded in Jerusalem in 1953 by Palestinian Islamic scholar Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani. Initially active in East Jerusalem, the organisation subsequently expanded its activities to dozens of countries, including Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, Egypt, Tunisia and Türkiye. According to publicly available sources, Hizb ut-Tahrir differs from other Islamist movements through its extensive ideological framework and its detailed vision of the political system it seeks to establish. The organisation is banned in several countries, including Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Russia, China and Uzbekistan. Members have been imprisoned in a number of these countries. Hizb ut-Tahrir is also officially banned in Azerbaijan. The protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara was held over claims of a hijab ban. The reported links between the platform that first circulated the footage and Hizb ut-Tahrir have drawn attention to the organisation behind the initial coverage of the demonstration. The available information does not establish whether Hizb ut-Tahrir organised the protest itself or had any direct involvement in arranging it. Tags: hijab Protests

https://www.azernews.az/nation/265504.ht.body: Azerbaijani MPs criticise Turkish authorities over anti-Azerbaijan statements 13 October 2026 17:35 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more The Milli Majlis working group on inter-parliamentary relations with Türkiye has issued a statement expressing concern over what it described as an anti-Azerbaijani campaign in Turkish media and social networks. The statement particularly criticised remarks made by certain members of Türkiye's ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) and Oktay Saral, chief adviser to the Turkish president, describing their accusations against Azerbaijan as unfounded. The Azerbaijani parliamentarians emphasised that the principle of “One nation, two states,” which underpins relations between Azerbaijan and Türkiye, does not grant either country the right to interfere in the other's internal affairs or impose its political and religious views. The working group also condemned insults directed at Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, the Azerbaijani people and the country's historical figures, describing such remarks as unacceptable. “Unfortunately, the AKP authorities are taking no steps to prevent all this,” the statement said. The parliamentarians also expressed concern over what they described as the Turkish authorities' tolerant attitude towards provocative actions taking place outside Azerbaijan's diplomatic missions in Türkiye. The statement called on representatives of Türkiye's ruling party to demonstrate political responsibility, respect Azerbaijan's sovereignty and constitutional order, and refrain from statements or actions that could damage relations between the two countries. Tags: AKP Milli Majlis (Parliament) of Azerbaijan Azerbaijan Turkey relations

The Azerbaijani Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) strongly condemns the fact that French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot once again targeted Azerbaijan with baseless allegations during his speech at the OECD (Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development) Global Forum on Building Trust and Reinforcing Democracy on October 13. This was stated by Foreign Ministry spokesperson Aykhan Hajizada in a commentary addressing allegations against Azerbaijan made by French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot at an OECD event. According to the statement, the French minister’s accusations against Azerbaijan demonstrate that the French side remains unwilling to abandon its confrontational rhetoric in relations with Azerbaijan. “Accusing Azerbaijan of interfering in the struggle for the rights of people living in New Caledonia and other French overseas territories is completely unfounded. The unfounded association of the parties’ differing positions on events taking place in France’s overseas territories with foreign interference is an attempt to overshadow the will and interests of the people of those territories. French officials who speak of democracy, human rights, and the rule of law would do well to focus first and foremost on consistently applying these principles in French politics. We call on the French side to put an end to unfounded allegations against Azerbaijan and to uphold the principles of mutual respect, sovereign equality and non-interference in internal affairs in international relations,” the commentary noted. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/society/.body: Home Azerbaijan Society Four major sports venues under construction in Karabakh – deputy minister Society News 14 October 2026 13:16 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. Four major sports facilities are being built in Azerbaijan’s liberated territories to promote youth development and encourage young people to engage in sports. These include the Imarat Stadium in Aghdam, a stadium in Khankendi, and sports infrastructure in Fuzuli and Zangilan, Deputy Minister of Youth and Sports Farhad Hajiyev said at a panel session titled “Youth in Karabakh’s Revival: Initiatives and Opportunities,” held as part of the Rebuild Karabakh exhibition during Caspian Construction Week, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. He said Karabakh had become one of the state’s priority areas. In this regard, involving young people in discussions on the region’s revival was a logical approach, as Karabakh’s future development depended on today’s youth. Hajiyev noted that Khankendi had now become a genuine city of young people. Although Mingachevir previously held this status, the large number of students and young people in Khankendi was now a source of particular joy. According to him, Khankendi and Karabakh as a whole were experiencing a new spring. The deputy minister called on everyone to visit the liberated territories, saying that such visits evoked unique emotions and a profound sense of pride. Hajiyev emphasized that the Ministry of Youth and Sports operated within the framework of the tasks set by the state and was responsible for implementing relevant decrees, orders, and programs signed by the president. In this regard, the part of the state program outlining socioeconomic development priorities through 2030 that focuses on human capital development was particularly important. According to him, numerous events were being held in Khankendi and other liberated territories under this program. Some of these initiatives were aimed at integrating the local population. The ministry was also seeking to organize international events in these territories wherever possible, with a target of holding approximately one in every three international events there. Hajiyev recalled that in 2024, Khankendi was named the Youth Capital of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation member states, and several international events were held in the city that year. He said the organizers sought to recruit young volunteers primarily from among local residents, while giving preference to young people from Karabakh when selecting participants. This approach helped promote their integration into society and provided opportunities for personal development. The deputy minister noted that sports were another key area of the Ministry of Youth and Sports’ work, adding that sports played an important role in maintaining physical health and mental well-being. Four major sports facilities are currently under construction in the liberated territories. According to him, the historic Imarat Stadium is being built in Aghdam, while renovation work at the stadium in Khankendi is nearing completion. Hajiyev recalled that a football match was held at the Khankendi stadium in 2023 in the presence of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, with the team of the Karabakh Central Army Sports Club also taking part. The stadium is now undergoing a complete renovation. In addition, large sports complexes are being built in Fuzuli and Zangilan. “I believe that once these sports facilities become operational, our young people will make active use of them, because a healthy mind resides in a healthy body,” the deputy minister said. Hajiyev also highlighted the various youth programs currently being implemented in Karabakh. He welcomed a proposal by Member of Parliament Shahin Seyidzade to establish a special grant program for young people living in the region. The deputy minister said that when he and Seyidzade worked at the Youth Foundation, a grant program for individuals had been implemented, and this work was continuing. In his view, the Karabakh Revival Foundation could also contribute to such initiatives, helping integrate local young people. The Ministry of Youth and Sports was ready to play an active role in this process. He also stressed the importance of winners of the “Yukselish” competition working in Karabakh. According to the deputy minister, several competition winners were already working in the region, which was a source of pride for them. Hajiyev noted that one of the winners, who had worked for an international organization, had recently moved to Karabakh University. Despite previously working at an international organization in central Baku, the individual had decided to teach at Karabakh University, pursue educational activities, and serve as a program director. The deputy minister described this as an example demonstrating that the “Yukselish” competition had been the right choice. He said that people’s values could not be measured solely in material terms, as moral values were also important. According to him, participants representing various institutions were actively providing support. The “Yukselish” team had visited Karabakh several times with competition winners and implemented projects in the region. A forum for competition winners is also planned to be held in Karabakh by the end of this year. Hajiyev emphasized that the main goal was to keep Karabakh a constant priority and ensure the active participation of people living in the region, particularly young people, in ongoing initiatives. He said participation in the competition was voluntary and no one could be forced to take part. Nevertheless, he said, it was desirable for people living in Karabakh to participate actively in such competitions. The possibility of holding a separate competition for university students in the future, aimed at identifying those with the strongest leadership potential, could also be considered. The deputy minister expressed hope that Karabakh University would play an active role in this process. At the end of his remarks, Hajiyev said he believed the Rebuild Karabakh exhibition would become a regular event and could eventually be held in Karabakh itself. “I believe this exhibition will become an annual tradition and one day may be held in Karabakh as well. I believe that day is not far away,” the deputy minister added. The event is being held at the Baku Expo Center from October 14 to 16 and includes four international exhibitions, alongside another international exhibition dedicated to road infrastructure and public transport. Caspian Construction Week serves as a platform for companies representing various industries to showcase their products and solutions, bring together sector participants, and establish professional contacts. The event covers several areas, ranging from construction materials and heating and ventilation equipment to solutions for Karabakh’s reconstruction, the plastics and polymer industries, road infrastructure, and public transport. The exhibitions held during the week provide local and international companies with opportunities to present their products and technologies, follow market developments, and discuss potential cooperation with prospective partners. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4234624..body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijan to cover 50% of grid fees from 2027 – deputy minister Azerbaijan News 14 October 2026 12:29 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Firaya Nurizada Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. Starting in 2027, the Azerbaijani state is set to cover 50% of electricity grid connection fees for industrial and agricultural facilities, First Deputy Minister of Economy Elnur Aliyev said at the 3rd National Competition Forum organized by the State Agency for Antimonopoly and Consumer Market Control, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. He said the measure would help reduce entrepreneurs’ initial investment burden. https://www.ng.ru/cis/2026-10-13/5_9602_.body: Президент Касым-Жомарт Токаев объявил о проведении досрочных выборов в местные органы власти. Фото с сайта www.akorda.kz Казахстан готовится к внеочередным выборам маслихатов – местных советов депутатов. Президент Касым-Жомарт Токаев 12 октября досрочно прекратил их полномочия и поручил Центризбиркому организовать голосование. По закону оно должно пройти в течение двух месяцев. Обновление местных советов станет следующей проверкой политической реформы. Директор центра актуальных исследований «Альтернатива» Андрей Чеботарев предполагает, что голосование состоится 6 декабря: предельный срок, 12 декабря, выпадает на субботу. Пока это экспертный прогноз. ЦИК не торопится с назначением даты досрочного голосования, ожидая, вероятно, послания Токаева. Президент обещал обозначить в нем цели и задачи на предстоящий период. Политолог Эдуард Полетаев связывает необходимость досрочных выборов с изменениями партийной системы: большинство местных депутатов избиралось от AMANAT («Доверие»), объявившей о присоединении к недавно созданной партии «Адилет» («Справедливость»). «Это закономерно поднимает вопрос о легитимности значительной части действующего депутатского корпуса», – считает эксперт. Это политическая оценка, которая сама по себе не означает юридической утраты мандатов. Полетаев считает обновление своевременным: «От их вердиктов зависят бюджеты, развитие городов и районов, а также решение многих вопросов, с которыми жители сталкиваются каждый день». Перестройка партийной системы уже отразилась на составе маслихатов. По подсчетам BES.media, опубликованным до указа об их роспуске, около 13 местных депутатов перешли в Курултай, еще примерно 9 сложили полномочия по другим причинам. Четыре депутата маслихата Алматы утратили мандаты после выхода из AMANAT, став кандидатами в Курултай от «Адилет». Аналогичная ситуация возникла у депутата Западно-Казахстанского областного маслихата Турарбека Тлемисова. В области Абай прекратились полномочия Эльзиры Солтабаевой, Съезбека Ахметова и Эрлана Батырбекова, также вошедших в список «Адилета». Партийная перестройка затронула юридические основания представительства. На референдуме 15 марта была принята новая Конституция, вступившая в силу 1 июля 2026 года. Двухпалатный парламент уступил место однопалатному Курултаю. Депутаты участвуют в согласовании ключевых назначений, включая премьер-министра и вице-президента. Однако президент сохраняет право освобождать их от должности, а повторный отказ согласовать кандидатуры может стать основанием для роспуска Курултая. На выборах 23 августа «Адилет» получила, по данным ЦИК, 71,17% голосов и 110 из 145 мандатов – почти 76% депутатских мест. Большинство может обходиться без поддержки меньшинства. Но это еще не означает независимости парламента. Ее практическим показателем станет готовность депутатов оспаривать решения исполнительной власти и добиваться их пересмотра. Оценки парламентской кампании расходятся. Председатель ЦИК Нурлан Абдиров заявил, что «были созданы комплексные условия для волеизъявления граждан». Международные наблюдатели в предварительном заключении БДИПЧ ОБСЕ отметили хорошую техническую подготовку, но недостаток политического плюрализма: все участвовавшие партии поддерживали курс президента. Они также указали на ограничения независимого выдвижения и нарушения при подсчете голосов. На местном уровне пространство для самостоятельного участия шире. В областных маслихатах, Астане, Алмате и Шымкенте (прежнее название Чимкент) половина депутатов избирается по партийным спискам, половина – по одномандатным округам. В районных и остальных городских маслихатах действует одномандатная система, допускающая самовыдвижение. В Курултай кандидаты проходят только через партии. Местная кампания проверит шансы независимых участников. Проверять результат реформы придется и на повседневных конфликтах. Работники Карагандинской сельскохозяйственной опытной станции имени А.Ф. Христенко заявили о многомесячной задержке зарплаты, об этом сообщила 12 октября общественная организация Казахстана «Фонд-бюро расследования коррупции» со ссылкой на медиаресурс msu.city. Речь идет о задолженности за июль и август в 52 млн тенге (9,7 млн руб.). Не добившись решения на уровне предприятия, сотрудники попросили президента Токаева вмешаться, организовать проверку и обеспечить выплаты. Одно обращение не характеризует настроения всего общества. Однако выбор адресата показателен: сотрудники связывают восстановление своих прав с вмешательством президента. Защиту трудовых прав должны обеспечивать инспекция, суд и профильные ведомства; депутаты могут добиваться их реакции. Пока для решения такой проблемы требуется публичная апелляция к главе государства, вопрос о действенности промежуточных институтов остается открытым. Политолог Досым Сатпаев еще в сентябре 2025 года, обсуждая парламентскую реформу, предлагал учитывать социальные критерии оценки власти: «насколько успешна борьба с инфляцией, растут ли зарплаты, будет ли возможность дать своим детям хорошее образование». Выборы маслихатов возвращают дискуссию к этим вопросам. Обновление депутатского корпуса приобретет смысл, если жители смогут защищать свои интересы через избранных представителей, не обращаясь каждый раз к президенту.

Они недоумевают, почему несколько лет назад они проливали кровь за свою страну, некоторые получили тяжелые ранения, в том числе лишились конечностей, а теперь их дочерям не дают учиться, потому что они мусульманки. Кроме того, в Сеть попало видео, записанное учительницей, на котором она при всем классе требует от девочки в возрасте семи-восьми лет снять платок. Ребенок плачет, но не подчиняется. На другом видео женщина стоит в школе возле доски с портретами солдат, погибших в карабахской войне, и требует либо допустить дочку к учебе, либо снять изображение ее отца. В первый же день, когда детей перестали пускать в школу, появились кадры штурма учебных заведений и как минимум одной сожженной машины директора. В результате массовых беспорядков было задержано не менее 37 человек. Им грозит до трех лет лишения свободы. «Главная цель этих мер... предотвратить перекрытие движения и нарушение нормального функционирования учебных заведений, а также обеспечить безопасность учащихся, преподавателей и других граждан», – говорится в заявлении МВД Азербайджана. Примечательно, что большинство СМИ республики полностью проигнорировали протесты. Пока в Баку дети и их родители осаждали школы, журналисты рассказывали о визите в республику премьер-министра Камбоджи Хун Манета. Однако те же самые издания во всех подробностях освещают протесты школьников во Франции, а саму Пятую республику обвиняют в империализме и неоколониализме. Тем временем председатель парламентского комитета по общественным объединениям и религиозным учреждениям Фазиль Мустафа считает, что ношение хиджаба в школе нужно было запретить, так как через него иностранные государства «отравляют» маленьких азербайджанцев своей идеологией. «После школы пусть тот, кто хочет, носит хиджаб, ведь на это нет запрета. К тому, что кто-то во дворе, дома, в месте поклонения, в мечети, на дороге, на улице носит, – к этому ведь нет возражений? Пойдите посмотрите на соседнюю страну – разве там сможешь пройти по улице без платка?» – добавил Мустафа. Глава телеканала Prime TV Айгун Мурадханли вовсе назвала протестующих родителей салафитами и агентами Ирана. «Протестующие против запрета на ношение хиджаба в школах – это в основном люди, связанные с Ираном. Другие протестующие – салафиты, и нет сомнений, что они также связаны с определенными центрами. Люди, которые раздувают эту проблему в социальных сетях, не заинтересованы в образовании своих детей, особенно девочек. Они даже не отправляют своих детей в школу. У них есть свои школы в садовых районах Баку. Все об этом знают, но почему-то правительство не знает», – сказала она. Глава центра политических исследований «Атлас» Эльхан Шахиноглу рассказал «НГ», что Азербайджан – светская мусульманская страна, в которой нет никаких проблем с исполнением религиозных обрядов, а количество мечетей постоянно растет. В то же время некоторые страны, включая Иран и Саудовскую Аравию, усиливают свое влияние на азербайджанских мусульман, подогревая среди них радикальные настроения. «В то время как Иран поддерживает шиитский радикализм в Азербайджане, Саудовская Аравия сыграла роль в формировании салафитского движения... Когда началась война в Сирии, некоторые выходцы из Азербайджана присоединились к местным террористам. В Иране сформировались радикальные религиозные группы, состоящие из бывших граждан Азербайджана, которые призывают к смене правительства в Баку и созданию исламской республики. Они пытаются влиять на религиозные семьи в Азербайджане через иранские веб-сайты... Азербайджанские власти и граждане, поддерживающие секуляризм, обеспокоены этим... С помощью запрета ношения хиджаба в школе можно идентифицировать радикальные силы. Религиозные семьи имеют два выбора: либо разрешить своим дочерям ходить в школу в форме, либо не отправлять детей в школу. Азербайджанское правительство не отступит», – сказал Шахиноглу. В свою очередь, кавказовед Владимир Новиков считает, что запрет хиджаба – часть борьбы с оппозиционными настроениями в Азербайджане. «Ранее президент Азербайджана Ильхам Алиев успешно решил для себя проблему светской оппозиции, но недовольные стали концентрироваться вокруг религии. Соответственно он атакует и в этом направлении, тем самым укрепляя свой режим. В то же время следует отметить, что этот процесс носит стихийный характер, но есть заинтересованные в нем игроки. Например, главный советник президента Турции Октай Сарал открыто выступил против запрета хиджаба. Кроме того, есть определенные брожения среди старых элит, сформировавшихся в период правления Гейдара Алиева. В целом сама по себе история с хиджабами вряд ли получит какое-то серьезное продолжение, но в Азербайджане, очевидно, сформировалась новая линия напряжения, которая еще даст о себе знать», – рассказал «НГ» Новиков.

Japan relies on journalists working in Russia to collect information intended to weaken Russia’s security, Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said. "Tokyo’s attempts to use its correspondents who are in Russia and have the status of foreign journalists to gather information with the aim of undermining the security of our state are regrettable. We cannot fail to point out that today’s event is not an isolated case," she said on the ministry’s website. https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/witnesse.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте Elie Wiesel , a survivor of Auschwitz and Buchenwald and the author of the well-known autobiographical novel Night, wrote that “only those who experienced Auschwitz know what it was; the rest will never know.” As Wiesel saw it, “the witness knew then, as he knows now,” that his experience could not be conveyed or fully comprehended by those who had not been in a concentration camp and had not endured torture and humiliation. The author of the testimony asks: “Others will not know, but will they be able to understand?” And yet, despite his doubts, Wiesel “simply could not remain silent.” Reflecting on the destruction of European Jewry by the German Nazis, Wiesel concludes that over the years not only the actions but also the aims of the antisemites changed: if at the beginning of their rule the Nazis set themselves the task of “building a society without Jews,” towards the end they wanted “to leave behind a world in which Jews seemed never to have existed at all.” Violence against people — Jewish men, women and children — was accompanied by the destruction of the very memory of this people, their culture, language and religion. For many witnesses, the struggle against the destruction of memory became the purpose of their lives, an act of resistance. Contemporary antifascists often repeat that “to remember means to resist,” holding events in memory of comrades killed by neo-Nazis. “Memory Is Resistance” is the slogan on the website of members of Memorial who study the history of political repression in the USSR and preserve testimonies of the horrors of the Soviet past. Memory matters to everyone: both to those who refuse to let themselves or others forget the crimes of the past and the suffering of the victims, and to those who take pride in that past. It is not simply a matter of knowing something — Wiesel was right about that — achieving understanding is much more difficult. We can see how declared aims and ideological attitudes continue to change in our own time. From “Holocaust denial” — until quite recently, apologists for German nationalism claimed that Jews had not been exterminated and had themselves invented both the camps and the crematoria in order to slander innocent Germans (there were even claims that Jews themselves had organised the mass murder of Jews to spite the Aryans) — to contemporary proposals by Alternative for Germany not to teach about Hitlerism in schools and instead devote more attention to Bismarck. Germany’s far-right politicians are now closer to the cynical attitude: “Here’s your beer, here’s your ham, and what happened yesterday is in the past” (the ever-relevant words of a song by Yuliy Kim). No one is saying that it did not happen: it did. The only question is how to regard it, how to understand it. The militarist and nationalist Bismarck is, for the AfD, something good, something to take pride in, while schoolchildren need not be told about certain costs of twentieth-century history: enough already, so much has been said about it. The lavish funeral held in Belgrade with military honours for Ratko Mladić, convicted by the Hague Tribunal of crimes against humanity, is a striking manifestation of the contemporary conflict over memory: for some, the victims and witnesses of crimes matter; for others, what matters is the glorification of war criminals. Everyone wants to remember — but they remember different things and understand the past differently. Those who are erecting ever more monuments to Stalin in the Russian Federation obviously want to remind people of him, often making no attempt to conceal the fact that Stalinism was terror. They simply like terror and want to put it back on a pedestal. And they are prepared to remember the Gulag as well — not to deny its existence, but to explain it in their own way, interpreting it within the framework of the “inadmissibility of distorting the history of the USSR.” Thus, for example, one can hold an academic conference in a former Soviet camp, highlighting “examples of the extraordinary courage and patriotism of our compatriots, whose military and labour achievements have more than once become a central theme of academic conferences organised for ten years by the Perm-36 Museum-Reserve.” But telling the history of the Stalinist era as it was seen by those who survived despite the terror, those who neither forgot nor forgave, is treated as extremism. This is why Memorial was banned and the Gulag History Museum in Moscow was closed. It is not memory that is forbidden — it is understanding that is forbidden, precisely what Elie Wiesel and many others sought to achieve through their testimonies. The struggle to foster an understanding that terror and war crimes are unacceptable does not end even when a verdict has been handed down by the Hague (or Nuremberg) Tribunal. Constant efforts are required not only to prevent people from forgetting, but also to show history — including the most recent history — through the eyes of victims of violence, those who suffered, and surviving witnesses. To show their truth rather than the perpetrator’s version: the perpetrator who does not even conceal what he is doing — who may even take pride in it — but who always has an explanation of his own, most often that he was forced to “strike first,” to assert his right to dominance, and so on. The perpetrators themselves are also eager to preserve the memory of violence — in military monuments, bas-reliefs and installations. The voices of those who suffered can be heard in their memories, accounts and testimonies, which must be collected and published, as is being done today by the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group’s “Voices of War” project and in human rights reports , which bring together the tragic experiences of Ukrainian women and men who have suffered as a result of Russia’s military aggression. Stephania KULAEVA First published on the Radio Svoboda blog Facebook Twitter Вконтакте

https://montenegro.osce.org/news/mission.body: News News Item OSCE-supported court simulation strengthens Montenegro’s judicial response to violence against women and girls Issued on: 13 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Montenegro Fields of work: Rule of law , Gender-based violence Strengthening the capacity of judicial professionals to handle cases of violence against women and girls in a victim-centered manner is essential to preventing secondary victimization and ensuring fair trials. As the OSCE Mission to Montenegro marks 20 years of co-operation with national institutions this year, it continues to support joint efforts to strengthen the institutional responses to such violence. In this context, the Mission, in co-operation with the Supreme Court and the Centre for Training in Judiciary and State Prosecution Service, organized a court simulation training in Budva from 9 to 11 October for 15 judicial and prosecutorial advisors on handling cases of violence against women and girls. Now in its fourth consecutive year, the simulation aims to strengthen institutional responses to violence against women and girls. Building on previous simulations on femicide, rape, stalking and marital rape, this year’s exercise focused on the practical application of international and national legal standards through a mock trial involving a case of violence against women and girls. Participants examined the key stages of criminal proceedings, including the assessment of evidence, the preparation of an indictment, the main hearing and the delivery of a judgment. Opening the event, Ms. Ljiljana Perkušić, Democratization Programme Manager of the OSCE Mission, highlighted the relevance of this year’s exercise in translating legal standards into practice, particularly in light of recent amendments to the Criminal Procedure Code, which further strengthen the victim-centered approach. Ms. Gordana Nikolić, Head of the Specialized Training Department at the Centre for Training in Judiciary and State Prosecution Service, expressed her gratitude to the Mission and the Supreme Court for their continued co-operation in organizing the training. She noted that the exercise provided valuable learning opportunities and contributed to reducing the risk of secondary victimization, while strengthening the capacity of the judiciary to address cases involving women who have experienced domestic violence. Ms. Bojana Bandović, advisor to the Supreme Court, noted that the simulation served as a platform for exchanging experiences and good practices, while also raising awareness of the complexity and seriousness of cases involving violence against women and girls. She emphasized the importance of addressing these cases without prejudice or stereotypes, with full respect for the dignity of victims and the principles of a fair trial. https://dushanbe.osce.org/news/programme.body: News News Item Young women from Tajikistan and Afghanistan explore leadership, diplomacy and peace through OSCE course From 5 to 9 October 2026, the OSCE held the second edition of its Advanced Course on Diplomacy, Leadership and Peace for Young Women in Dushanbe, fostering collaboration among 20 young women from Tajikistan and Afghanistan to strengthen their leadership skills and prepare them to contribute to diplomacy and peacebuilding. Issued on: 13 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe Fields of work: Gender equality , Youth From 5 to 9 October 2026, the OSCE held the second edition of its Advanced Course on Diplomacy, Leadership and Peace for Young Women in Dushanbe, fostering collaboration among 20 young women from Tajikistan and Afghanistan to strengthen their leadership skills and prepare them to contribute to diplomacy and peacebuilding. The course aimed to equip participants with the knowledge, practical skills and professional networks needed to take an active role in promoting peace and security across the OSCE region and beyond. Through peer-to-peer learning, intergenerational dialogue and discussions with experienced guest speakers, participants explored a range of issues, including artificial intelligence and diplomacy, peacebuilding, human rights, career development and resilience. They also exchanged experiences and discussed the challenges and opportunities facing young women pursuing careers in these fields. Parvathy Ramaswami (centre), United Nations Resident Coordinator in Tajikistan, leads the “Coffee Talk” session on Diplomacy, Leadership, and the Next Generation as part of the OSCE’s Advanced Course on Diplomacy, Leadership and Peace for Young Women, Dushanbe, 5 October 2026. “Today, Tajik women are not merely participants in political processes, but active, thoughtful and responsible contributors to public life, embodying national values and a culture of peace, dialogue and constructive co-operation,” said Mavsuma Muini, Deputy Chairperson of the Majlisi Namoyandagon, the lower chamber of Tajikistan’s Parliament. “The OSCE School of Diplomacy, Leadership and Peacebuilding for Young Women is a valuable initiative that helps promote women’s participation in diplomacy and public and political life and raise the status of women in society,” Muini added. Fejzo Numanaj, Acting Deputy Head of Office and Officer-in-Charge of the OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe, encouraged participants to recognize their leadership potential: “You are not the leaders of tomorrow. You are already leaders today, in your universities, your workplaces, and your communities.” He added: “Together with the Parliament of Tajikistan, the Government, the United Nations and civil society, we remain committed to ensuring that young women’s voices shape dialogue, decisions and solutions.” Group photo marking the launch of the OSCE’s second Advanced Course on Diplomacy, Leadership and Peace for Young Women, featuring 20 young women from Tajikistan and Afghanistan alongside senior women leaders from the Government of Tajikistan and representatives of international organizations, Dushanbe, 5 October 2026. The course concluded with participants expanding their professional networks and reaffirming their commitment to contributing to peace and security. By investing in young women’s leadership and fostering dialogue across generations, the OSCE seeks to promote their meaningful participation in diplomacy and peacebuilding and enable them to contribute to addressing shared security challenges. https://rfom.osce.org/representative-fre.body: Press release OSCE RFoM organized the 26th Central Asia Media Conference in Bishkek, held bilateral meetings with Kyrgyz authorities Date: 13 October 2026 Place: BISHKEK Source: OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media BISHKEK, 13 October 2026 – The OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, in co-operation with OSCE field operations in the region, organized the 26 th Central Asia Media Conference in Bishkek on 9 and 10 October gathering participants from Central Asia, Mongolia and the broader OSCE region. Interactive discussions focused on information integrity and trusted information landscapes in the region, safety of journalists, legislative and regulatory frameworks, journalism education, and professional standards. The conference was opened by the OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, Ambassador Jan Braathu; Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic Kairat Tursunkulov; Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy of the Kyrgyz Republic Salkyn Sarnogoeva; and the Head of the OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek, Ambassador Volker Frobarth. “There are multiple challenges journalists face in their work throughout the OSCE region, including Central Asia. However, our responses to these challenges must remain firmly grounded in fundamental rights, including freedom of expression and media freedom. Open discussion about the importance of media freedom and its impact on our common security is crucial,” Ambassador Braathu said in his opening remarks. During his visit to Bishkek, Representative Braathu held bilateral meetings with the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic, Kairat Tursunkulov; the First Deputy Minister of Justice, Saira Yzakova; and the Chairman of the Service for Regulation and Supervision in the Communication Sector under the Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies, Altynbek Toktorbaev. On 10 and 11 October, the Office of the OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media partnered with the Bishkek Academy for the Academy’s annual alumni conference focussing on “Artificial Intelligence, Climate Change and Sustainable Development”. The RFoM Office’s work in the areas of media and AI was discussed at the conference within the Central Asian framework. The Office also laid out strategies to promote stronger climate and environmental journalism, and presented the RFoM/UNESCO joint publication “ Reporting the Environment: A Practical Manual for Journalists ”. Furthermore, the conference provided an opportunity to present the translation of OSCE Ministerial Council Decision No. 3/18 on the Safety of Journalists into five Central Asian languages and Mongolian, and discuss the implementation of the principles included in the Decision. “A commitment adopted at the international level needs to reach the people and institutions that are in a position to give it practical effect. And that means bringing the commitment not only geographically closer, but also linguistically closer, to those stakeholders. This is why translating MC Decision 3/18 into Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tajik, Turkmen, Uzbek and Mongolian is part of the implementation process and a step towards national ownership,” concluded Braathu. The OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media observes media developments in all 57 OSCE participating States. He provides early warning on violations of freedom of expression and media freedom and promotes full compliance with OSCE media freedom commitments. https://odihr.osce.org/news/odihr/668634.body: News News Item ODIHR and OSCE PA launch guidelines to strengthen participation of people with disabilities in parliaments Issued on: 12 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights , OSCE Parliamentary Assembly Fields of work: Democratization , Tolerance and non-discrimination The OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) and the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly (OSCE PA) launched a new publication in Warsaw on 12 October 2026 to help parliaments identify and remove barriers to the full and effective participation of people with disabilities. People with disabilities remain underrepresented in national parliaments across the OSCE region and continue to face barriers to participation. Addressing these barriers means examining how people can contribute to parliamentary work, influence legislation and hold governments to account, alongside ensuring access to parliamentary buildings and information. “People with disabilities must be able to shape the laws and decisions that affect their lives. Parliaments need to examine their own rules and practices and work with people with disabilities to remove barriers to participation,” said Zaruhi Batoyan, Member of the National Assembly of the Republic of Armenia. Guidelines on Advancing disability-inclusive parliaments: an assessment methodology and insights from the OSCE region draws on a joint ODIHR/OSCE PA survey conducted in 2024. It combines survey findings and examples of good practice with a methodology covering representation, law-making, oversight and access, helping parliaments identify priorities and take practical steps towards reform. “Accessibility is part of everyday parliamentary work, from receiving information to taking part in debates and committee meetings. The test is whether people with disabilities can contribute on equal terms and have their voices reflected in decisions,” said Dastan Bekeshev, Member of the Jogorku Kenesh of the Kyrgyz Republic. Parliamentarians and civil society representatives shared experiences from the OSCE region and discussed how the methodology can be applied in practice. The publication was launched at a side event organized by ODIHR and the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly during the 2026 Warsaw Human Dimension Conference . https://hcnm.osce.org/news/hcnm/668601.body: News News Item OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities visits Kosovo Issued on: 12 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities Fields of work: Conflict prevention and resolution , Human rights , National minority issues , Tolerance and non-discrimination , Gender equality OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities Christophe Kamp visited Kosovo on 9 October 2026 to exchange with central and local authorities on recent developments that affected the situation of non-majority communities. In Prishtinë/Priština, Kamp met with Prime Minister Albin Kurti to continue their conversation on the importance of finding effective modalities to consult non-majority communities on policies and issues affecting them. The High Commissioner also met with the Mayor of North Mitrovica, Milan Radojević, to discuss recent developments in his municipality, particularly related to property rights and dialogue between central and local authorities. Kamp also held an exchange of views with the heads of KFOR, EULEX, the EU Office, and UNMIK. Стороны наметили подготовку совместной программы действий на период 2028–2034 годов. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/10/13/politbl.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp МВД Кыргызстана сообщило о задержании Сыргака Кенжебаева, автора youtube-канала «Эр-Сыргак» — последнюю пару месяцев он критиковал власть и рассказывал, как сотрудничал с братом президента Садыра Жапарова Сабыром. По его словам Сабыр Джапаров вместе с сыном в своем «офисе» решал «политические вопросы» и влиял на таможню. МВД подозревает Кенжебаева в призывах к массовым беспорядкам и мошенничестве. Якобы Кенжебаев взял у некой М.Н. 150 тысяч долларов для совместной предпринимательской деятельности. Его объявили в розыск. Ведомство настаивает, что за границей Кенжебаев скрывался от уголовного преследования, и публиковал «провокационные материалы». По версии следствия, он призывал к массовым беспорядкам и последующему захвату власти. Не первое похищение за границей Задержание Кенжебаева, находившегося за границей, и последующий вывоз в Кыргызстан — не первая попытка лишить его свободы. И у его задержаний всегда кроме обвинения, которое в его адрес озвучивает следствие, есть и политическая подоплека. На данный период — его критика власти и объявление себя оппозицией Садыру Жапарову. Ранее Кенжебаев уже сообщал, что власти пытались задержать его в Камбодже 31 августа. Тогда он в одном из стримов сообщил, что на его задержание со своими подчиненными прибыл лично начальник главного управления уголовного розыска МВД Улан Айтбаев. Вместе с ним на пяти джипах приехали местная полиция, сотрудники спецслужб и консульства. Матраимов после задержания, 2024 год. А вот предыдущее задержание Кенжебаева было связано с противостоянием с экс-зампредом кыргызской таможни Райымбеком Матраимовым. Сыргак Кенжебаев — бизнесмен, создавший таможенный терминал «Юнилаб». Изначально проект выглядел многообещающим, но столкнулся с искусственно созданными проблемами, после которых новыми владельцами терминала стали люди из окружения экс-зампреда таможни Райымбека Матраимова . Бизнес-партнер Кенжебаева описал ту сделку как «рейдерский захват». Когда бывшая супруга Кенжебаева экс-депутатка Ширин Айтматова начала антикоррупционную кампанию против Райымбека Матраимова, Кенжебаева похитили из Алматы и оставили под арестом в Кыргызстане . Тогда следствие настаивало, что его задержали за якобы мошенничество. Заявление на него написал гражданин Китая, уверявший, что Кенжебаев завладел 350 000 долларов. По словам Айтматовой, это был некий Муталиф, китайский бизнесмен уйгурского происхождения. Она подозревала, что он из корпорации АКА, с ним Кенжебаева познакомил депутат Алиарбек Абжалиев, сват тогдашнего президента Сооронбая Жээнбекова. У президента Жапарова хорошие отношения с Абдукадыром. Вот они вместе на церемонии начала строительства дорогущей мечети в пригороде Бишкека. Корпорация «АКА» принадлежит Хабибулле Абдукадыру — влиятельному китайскому бизнесмену и герою журналистского расследования о контрабанде. Он сват Райымбека Матраимова и так или иначе взаимодействовал с тремя последними кыргызскими президентами — Алмазбеком Атамбаевым, Сооронбаем Жээнбековым и Садыром Жапаровым. Ради безопасности Кенжебаева Айтматова прекратила публичную деятельность. Кенжебаев смог выйти на свободу только после протестов в октябре 2020 года, когда протестующие освободили Садыра Жапарова. Однако в том же месяце всех освобожденных вернули в колонию — кроме Садыра Жапарова. Спустя какое-то время Кенжебаева все же освободили и он, по его словам, пытался сотрудничать с властью по привлечению в Кыргызстан инвестиций — факт коммуникации с Кенжебаевым подтвердил Садыр Жапаров. В начале августа Кенжебаев открыл канал на YouTube и начал публиковать видеоролики о происходящем в Кыргызстане. В одном из них он рассказал, что Сабыр Джапаров и Рустам Жапаров, брат и сын президента, а также другие его близкие родственники, якобы «решают политические вопросы Кыргызстана» и контролируют таможню из так называемого «офиса». При этом Сабыр Джапаров и другие близкие родственники президента никогда официально не занимали никакие госдолжности. Брат президента «Сабыр Джапаров там уселся и организовал офис. И не только он. Братья и члены семьи Жапаровых обосновались там. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/10/13/po-puti.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Когда полгода назад налоговая выпустила расследование о клане Ташиевых и схемах на «Кыргызнефтегазе», невольно появлялся вопрос — не будут ли авторов расследования преследовать также, как и авторов другого расследования на ту же тему? Еще в 2022 году, 20 января, издание «Temirov Live» рассказало о «схеме Ташиевых» , которая позволила заработать компании, связанной с главой ГКНБ Камчыбеком Ташиевым, 37 млн сомов всего за два дня. 22 января журналист-расследователь Болот Темиров был задержан , а правоохранители подкинули ему наркотики, которые потом сами же и нашли. В тот же день Камчыбек Ташиев обвинил журналистов расследователей во лжи. 23 января Ташиев даже дал пресс-конференцию, где на доске подробно объяснил, как работает предприятие по продаже мазута. Само расследование стало предтечей масштабного давления на всю команду журналистов, насильного изгнания Темирова из страны и массовых арестов сотрудников. Но расследование налоговой, опубликованное после освобождения Камчыбека Ташиева с его должностей, привело к допросам и арестам фигурантов дела. Однако, полгода спустя публикации лицо и автор расследования Анарбек Катаганов рассказал — его тоже преследовали за расследование о Ташиевых. Более того, его даже задерживали — однако задержание официально связано с пострадавшим во время штурма резиденции бывшего президента Алмазбека Атамбаева милиционером Саматом Курманкуловым. « Вся эта история — спланированная провокация из-за моего расследования про «Кыргызнефтегаз» и семью Ташиевых. С момента выхода видео мне поступали угрозы, а затем меня попытались сломать через грязную подставу со старым делом 2015 года и 1,5-минутным звонком генералу Самату Курманкулову, которого использовали вслепую. Силовики сработали по ложному доносу мгновенно », — рассказал Катаганов в своих соцсетях. Подробнее он рассказал в приложенном к посту интервью. Если опустить детали, получается что Катаганова задержали за звонок Курманкулову, а после выхода из СИЗО источник сообщил ему, что все это связано с Ташиевыми. Катаганов объясняет — ему после выхода видео налоговой угрожали, говорили «зачем ты снял про Ташиева, он наш брат». По его словам, в Жалал-Абаде его «вообще убить хотели». А вот задержанного по делу о «Кыргызнефтегазе» брата Камчыбека Ташиева Шайырбека Ташиева, отпустили под домарест в июле. Источники до того сообщали СМИ, что Шайырбек Ташиев ни дня не провел в СИЗО-1, куда был определен судом. Вместо этого он был в ИВС ГУВД Бишкека. Еще в апреле МВД сообщало, что задержанный сегодня по делу «Кыргызнефтегаза» экс-депутат Шайырбек Ташиев должен возместить государству за нанесенный ущерб 4,1 млрд сомов. Это порядка 46 млн долларов. И президент комментировал это дело — Садыр Жапаров сказал , что Шайырбек Ташиев «должен все вернуть», и только потом выйдет на свободу. Только вот в сентябре от адвоката Ташиева Жыргалбека Бабаева стало известно , что сумму ущерба пересмотрят. МВД сообщило, что Шайырбек Ташиев возместил «основную часть ущерба» — однако сумму не назвали. https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/khpg-new.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте A roundup of news from the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group (KHPG), one of the oldest human rights organizations in Ukraine. Since 2014, KHPG has been documenting war crimes in eastern Ukraine, and since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, it has been documenting events that show signs of crimes under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes) across all regions of Ukraine. KHPG is one of the founders of the T4P (Tribunal for Putin) initiative, which brings together more than two dozen organizations with the aim of holding Russia accountable for the crimes committed. Russian Education as a Tool for Militarization In occupied Crimea, discussions are underway about the operation of cadet and “Cossack” classes for schoolchildren, the expansion of the “Little Cadets and Cossacks” project for preschoolers, the role of military training camps, and cooperation between Crimean schools and the Russian occupation security agencies. Thirteen kindergartens, with groups of children aged five to seven, are participating in the propaganda project “Little Cadets and Cossacks.” In the temporarily occupied territories of Donetsk Oblast, Russian paratroopers have organized an event where they demonstrated military equipment to minors. In occupied Skadovsk, cadets at School No. 1 were provided with uniforms for classes operating under the patronage of Rosgvardiya (the Russian National Guard). In effect, schoolchildren will be wearing uniforms resembling those of Russian security forces. “The problem is not only that military culture is being imposed on children. The use of uniforms closely resembling those worn by Russian security forces creates a dangerous situation under conditions of occupation and hostilities: it becomes significantly more difficult to distinguish civilian children from members of Russian security forces,” the Ukrainian National Resistance Center notes. In an overview article, KHPG examines the ongoing militarization and indoctrination of Ukrainian children by the occupying power. Read in Ukrainian: Російська освіта як плацдарм для мілітаризації A Family Affair: Russia Persecutes Entire Families in Occupied Territories Russian authorities widely employ the practice of detaining entire families in occupied territories. This makes it easier for Russian security services to exert pressure on those who oppose the regime. When charges are based on self-incriminating statements, detainees can be forced to sign virtually any testimony if their mother, son, or daughter is being held in a neighboring cell. KHPG recounts the persecution of seven families: Valentyn Maliar and his sister Tetiana Behei (Maliar), together with their children Anatolii Rossikhin and Olha Behei; married couple Serhii Kozlov and Yevheniia Samoilova; Viktoriia Strilets and her daughter Oleksandra Strilets; Oleksii Demianenko and his daughter Anzhelika Demianenko; Anna Murdidi, her son Artem Murdidi and his wife Anna Voshkoder; married couple Oleh Platonov and Nataliia Poliukh; and Volodymyr Perzhynskyi and his son Mark Perzhynskyi. Read in Ukrainian: Справи сімейні: росіяни переслідують на окупованих територіях цілі родини Detention Extended for Women Charged in the “First Female Hizb ut-Tahrir Case” Four Crimean Tatar women arrested a year ago, on October 15, 2025—Esma Nimetullaeva, Nasibe Saidova, Elviza Alieva, and Fevzie Osmanova—have had their pre-trial detention extended. It was previously reported that FSB officers had completed the “preliminary investigation” into the case of the Crimean detainees. According to sources, in addition to Article 205.5 of the Russian Criminal Code (concerning involvement in the activities of Hizb ut-Tahrir), the Crimean Tatar women are charged with preparing to seize power by force under Article 278 of the Russian Criminal Code. Esma Nimetullaeva , who lived in Bakhchysarai, worked as a pastry chef and was raising five underage daughters. Her husband, Crimea Solidarity activist Remzi Nimetullaev, was first detained in November 2021 in Sevastopol, when he came to meet a lawyer outside a detention center following the lawyer’s release from administrative detention. Remzi Nimetullaev was detained for a second time in August 2023, following a wave of mass searches. This time, he and five other Crimea Solidarity activists were accused of organizing the activities of Hizb ut-Tahrir. Elviza Alieva worked as a cashier at a bakery in Simferopol. She was also a fourth-year Management student at the so-called Crimean Federal University. Nasibe Saidova , the daughter of a well-known imam in Crimea, was in her final year of college, studying education, and worked with a nursery group at a kindergarten. Fevzie Osmanova worked in the family business, a shop. According to the Crimean Tatar Resource Center, as of March 2026, at least 52 women were known to have been subjected to political persecution by the Russian authorities and were being held in pre-trial detention centers or penal colonies. More details are available in the KHPG article. Read in English: Russia’s ‘trial’ begins of Crimean Tatar mother of five and three young women for ‘trying to violently seize power’ Analytical report within the framework of the KHPG project ‘Strengthening Public Oversight and Accountability of State Institutions in Ukraine’, 2025–2026 KHPG has published three sections of a comprehensive study on the human rights situation in Ukraine in 2025–2026, covering trends under wartime conditions, challenges in combating corruption, and the protection of the rights of vulnerable groups. The study traces developments in human rights protection in Ukraine from the beginning of the Russian-Ukrainian war in 2014, examines changes following the full-scale invasion in February 2022, and identifies trends in 2025–2026. Key issues addressed in the report: The report examines the narrowing of the space for civil and political freedoms under the pretext of martial law, the absence of systematic dialogue between the authorities and civil society, pressure on the opposition and attempts to subordinate the judiciary. It analyses the unconstitutional application of National Security and Defence Council (NSDC) sanctions against Ukrainian citizens and cases of unlawful deprivation of citizenship without transparent procedures or judicial oversight. In the sphere of freedom of speech, the report records the growing state monopolisation of the information space through the retention of the ‘United News Telethon’, the removal of patriotic opposition TV channels ( Espreso, Priamyi, Channel 5 ) from digital broadcasting, and pressure by law enforcement and security agencies (the SBU and the SBI) on investigative journalists and bloggers (the cases of Bihus.Info, Yu. Butusov, B. Bereza and Slidstvo.Info ). At the same time, it emphasises that society has retained its capacity for peaceful resistance (the ‘cardboard protests’ of 2025–2026). The third section of the report, “Human Rights in Ukraine 2025 and the First Half of 2026. Rights of Vulnerable Groups”, analyzes the situation of vulnerable groups in Ukraine during the war in 2025–2026, including sex workers, people who use drugs, women living with HIV, and LGBTIQ+ people. It highlights systemic discrimination, barriers to healthcare, legal challenges and recommendations. Monitoring networks continue to document hate speech, discrimination, harassment, and intolerance-motivated offences against LGBTIQ+ people based on sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC). At the same time, significant progress has been made in recognizing the situation and needs of LGBTIQ+ people as a social group in legislation and public policy. The number of legal and regulatory acts explicitly prohibiting discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation and/or gender identity has been steadily increasing.

https://www.rferl.org/a/germany-trial-no.body: Ukraine Germany To Start Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities' By Ray Furlong and RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service October 13, 2026 09:09 CET Germany To Start Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities' Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Policemen escort Serhii K. to a hearing with a prosecutor in Karlsruhe, Germany, on November 28, 2025. After four years of speculation, leaks, and briefings by anonymous sources, the world is finally about to hear evidence given publicly under oath in a German courtroom about how the Nord Stream gas pipelines were blown up -- in a case that could prove politically explosive. German prosecutors have identified seven Ukrainian suspects, but just one of them is in the dock in the trial beginning on October 14. He is named as Serhii K. in court documents that say he is suspected of a being an accomplice to a war crime. That classification has caused outrage. But German prosecutors have further raised the stakes by stating the suspects were operating "on behalf of state authorities in Ukraine." SEE ALSO: Ukrainian Arrested In Connection To 2022 Nord Stream Explosions Kyiv has always strictly denied any involvement in the attack, which damaged crucial energy infrastructure serving Germany -- one of its most important military backers in its fight since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Serhii K., who has been identified elsewhere as Serhiy Kuznetsov, says he is innocent. 'Two Crazy Military Men' Nord Stream is majority-owned by Russia's state-controlled Gazprom and co-financed by major European energy companies. It was constructed to deliver Russian gas directly to Germany, bypassing transit states such as Ukraine and Poland, which had tense relations with Moscow. The suspected sabotage and subsequent gas leaks happened in September 2022, rendering the pipelines as inoperable. Western governments originally accused Russia of carrying out the blasts, but German investigators started forming a case that said a group of Ukrainian divers hired a yacht and planted explosives on the seabed. They say Kuznetsov, a former military officer, was the ringleader. "At the end of February 2022, he and other military personnel, on behalf of state authorities in Ukraine, developed the plan," says a summary of the indictment released by prosecutors. "The aim was to permanently halt gas deliveries via the pipelines and prevent Russia from using the revenue from the natural gas trade to finance its war efforts." The prosecutors have not stated publicly the full extent of the alleged conspiracy. The full indictment contains some further details, according to three German media outlets that say they have seen it: public-service TV station ARD and two print-era heavyweights, Sueddeutsche Zeitung and Die Zeit. SEE ALSO: Ukraine Grants Bail To Military Officer Who Reportedly 'Coordinated' Nord Stream Sabotage They all reported that, while in custody in Italy, Kuznetsov had phoned his wife in Kyiv and investigators were secretly listening in as he said he'd been advised by a lawyer that it was time to admit this had been "an official military operation." His commander should state that they were not just "two crazy military men." Kuznetsov's Italian lawyer, Nicola Canestrini, has played down the importance of this evidence, saying there was "no smoking gun" in the case. "It is hard to believe that, after Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine, a German court should hold a war crimes trial against a Ukrainian serviceman," he added in comments to RFE/RL. The three German media outlets named Roman Chervinskiy as Serhii K.'s commander, and his name also appeared in multiple earlier media reports citing intelligence sources. Chervinskiy told RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service in July that "the Germans actually have no evidence whatsoever that Serhii took part in this operation, if it even took place." Another suspect, identified by Germany as Vladimir Z. , is currently in custody in Croatia, where he is fighting extradition. He was previously detained in Poland but was freed when a Polish judge ruled that if Ukraine were responsible for the Nord Stream attack, it was a "just" act. A professional diver identified by his Polish lawyers as Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, he was working in Croatia as an adviser on a Hollywood movie about Nord Stream. During the trial, the prosecution will have to lay out its evidence for a conspiracy and the full extent of it. "That is the crucial question: How much came from the top of the Ukrainian political system or how much was prepared by some insiders in the intelligence service?" Stefan Meister, a specialist on Russia and Eastern Europe at the German Council on Foreign Relations, told RFE/RL. SEE ALSO: Exclusive: A Russian Blueprint For A Cold, Dark Winter In Ukraine "The key political question is the role of Zelenskyy and the presidential administration. And there we still have no proof that they were really involved," he added. Kuznetsov's German lawyer, Jes Meyer-Lohkamp, said prosecutors "have not provided any direct, conclusive evidence of our client's involvement" and that the German court will have to determine whether Nord Stream was actually a legitimate military target. The Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg has scheduled two hearings every week until at least February, with no specified end date yet. German Support For Ukraine As the case unfolds, it will also feed into bitter disputes in Germany about ongoing support for Ukraine. The main opposition party, Alternative for Germany (AfD), is highly critical of this support and calls for close ties to Russia instead. Evidence of Ukrainian involvement in the Nord Stream attack "would strengthen the AfD's argumentation against this support for Ukraine," said Meister. "They have all these narratives about Ukrainian corruption, a failed state.... It would resonate also in parts of German society." The AfD has recently won key regional elections and is piling the pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government over Ukraine, immigration, and economic concerns. Merz's response has been to double-down on his current policies, including on Ukraine. Most recently, he was in Kyiv on October 4 with a new aid package including joint production of interceptors to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones. Mikhaylo Honchar, head of the Kyiv-based Strategy XXI Global Studies Center, told RFE/RL this would likely continue regardless of what comes out at the trial. "If you take into consideration real Russian policy, which is directed against the EU and NATO, and Russia's anti-German rhetoric, I think the government of Germany will avoid steps which would undermine the bilateral relationship" with Ukraine, he said. He added that the prosecution case was "absurd," citing German media reports that the attack may have been a Russian false-flag operation. But in any case, Honchar said, a guilty verdict would be met with a clear response in Ukraine. "Many people will say: 'If our guys did it, they are heroes.'" I'm RFE/RL Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak, and this week I am drilling down on one issue: the upcoming EU summit, with a focus on Ukraine, Russia sanctions, and EU enlargement.
